source: SAML-D — Oztas et al., IEEE ICEBE 2023. Third-party synthetic AML dataset.
why_this_matters: Everything rings.py had been measured against was planted by our own generator and found by our own code. This is independent ground truth with named typologies.

finding_1_community_detection_fails_and_.verdict: rings.py does not flag SAML-D's rings, and correctly so.
finding_1_community_detection_fails_and_.explanation: A conductance of ~0.99 means each ring member carries roughly 200 transactions of which only 1-2 are ring edges. The laundering is ~1% of that account's activity. No community method separates such a group, and the CONDUCTANCE_CEILING gate rejects them rather than manufacturing confidence.
finding_1_community_detection_fails_and_.component_structure: The rings are real and ring-sized — 38-52 connected components of 10-16 accounts per typology — they are simply not separable from the surrounding traffic.

finding_3_two_of_our_own_hypotheses_fail: Blending every motif into one score gives 12.4x lift. FAN_OUT alone gives 28.3x at 62% recall. Averaging a strong detector with weak ones destroys it.

Amount uniformity was expected to separate a laundering split from a payroll run. It does not: filtering to the most uniform fan-outs LOWERS precision from 11.2% to 9.0% and cuts recall from 62% to 11%. Value conservation on gather-scatter behaved the same way. Both are still reported as evidence for an investigator; neither is used to gate.
thresholds_were_not_tuned: WINDOW_DAYS, MIN_LEGS, MAX_CV and CONSERVATION_TOL are round numbers fixed before this benchmark and left alone after it. Tuning them here would produce a detector that scores on SAML-D.
